# Overview
This is a direct port of the retail **[RCLootCouncil](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/rclootcouncil)** addon with certain elements modified to fit within the Classic environment. This means this version can always be (mostly) up to date with the latest features added to the main addon. For the retail version and description, see the original **[RCLootCouncil](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/rclootcouncil)** addon.

### Wiki

The [RCLootCouncil Wiki](https://github.com/evil-morfar/RCLootCouncil2/wiki) contains all the information you may need to use the addon, along with examples of specific use cases and is up to date with the Classic version. Do check it out!

Create an issue [here on Curseforge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/rclootcouncil-classic/issues/create) , and make sure to follow the description.

Gargul is a loot add-on for classic and classic TBC that helps you pick up and distribute loot effortlessly and also allows you to distribute loot on-the-fly without having to take any breaks.

You can find Gargul on CurseForge here: <https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gargul> Also be sure to stop by our discord: <https://discord.com/invite/D3mDhYPVzf>

**Some of Gargul's features include**  
\- Auto looting (safe to use with recipes, nether vortex, splinter of atiesh etc.)  
\- Loot announcements and roll tracking  
\- Full support for softres.it and thatsmybis.com  
\- Loot trade timers so you never forget to roll out an item  
\- Auto inviting and group sorting based on input from raid-helper, the wowhead comp tool or your own excel/google sheets!

The auto looting also supports multiple "packmules" to quickly distribute disenchantables, mark of the illidari, word of thawing etc.

results.title: RCLootCouncil vs Gargul Which WoW Loot Addon Should You Use | by rengo | Medium
excerpts:
The two heavyweights in this space are RCLootCouncil and Gargul, and they approach the problem from completely different angles.

In this guide, you’ll learn:

* The fundamental philosophy behind each addon
* Detailed feature breakdowns with real testing results
* Which addon works best for different guild types
* Setup and configuration walkthroughs
* Common mistakes to avoid with each system
* My honest verdict after using both extensively

This guide is for raid leaders, loot council members, guild officers, and anyone who’s ever wanted to strangle someone over loot distribution.

## Understanding Loot Distribution Systems in 2026

Before we compare these addons, let’s talk about why loot distribution matters more than ever. With WoW Classic’s continued popularity and retail’s personal loot changes over the years, guilds have more options than ever for handling drops.

The two main approaches are:
Loot Council — A group of trusted players decides who gets each piece based on factors like attendance, performance, current gear, and raid needs. This is where RCLootCouncil shines.

Soft Reserve and Roll Systems — Players pre-select items they want, and when those items drop, reserved players get priority. Everyone else can roll. This is Gargul’s bread and butter.

Neither system is inherently better. It depends entirely on your guild’s culture, size, and goals.

## RCLootCouncil Deep Dive

Press enter or click to view image in full size

## What It Is

RCLootCouncil has been the gold standard for organized loot council guilds since its creation. It’s a comprehensive system that allows council members to vote on loot distribution, track history, and make informed decisions based on detailed player data.

## Why It Stands Out

...

History Tracking — Every piece of loot awarded is logged with timestamps, who received it, and what they said they’d use it for. This is invaluable when someone claims they “never get loot.”

Export Options — Data can be exported to spreadsheets for analysis. Some guilds track loot distribution over entire tiers to ensure fairness.

Gear Comparison — The addon shows item level comparisons so council can see if something is actually an upgrade or if the player is just being greedy.

Auto-Pass Options — Players can set up auto-pass rules for items they don’t need, reducing clutter in the voting window.

## Pros

* Industry standard for serious loot council guilds
* Extremely detailed tracking and history
* Voting system creates accountability
* Highly customizable response options
* Excellent documentation and community support

## Cons

* Steeper learning curve for new users
* Requires buy-in from entire raid team
* Can feel bureaucratic for casual guilds
* Setup takes significant time investment
* Overkill for smaller groups or pugs

## Best For

Established guilds with dedicated raid teams, progression-focused groups where loot optimization matters, and any guild that’s had loot drama and needs a transparent system.

## Gargul Deep Dive

Press enter or click to view image in full size

## What It Is

Gargul is a more flexible loot distribution addon that excels at soft reserve integration, GDKP support, and streamlined roll tracking. It’s designed to make the master looter’s life easier without requiring complex setup.

## Why It Stands Out

Where RCLootCouncil is about structured decision-making, Gargul is about speed and automation. It integrates directly with softres.it and thatsmybis.com, automatically tracks rolls, and handles the tedious parts of loot distribution so you can focus on actually raiding.

## My Testing Experience

I switched to Gargul for a Classic raid team running soft reserve, and the difference was immediate.

...

You’ll never accidentally let an item become unshareable again.

Roll Tracking — Automatically captures /roll results, sorts them highest to lowest, and shows if someone rolled multiple times.

GDKP Support — Built-in tools for gold-bid runs, though that’s less relevant in 2026’s Classic landscape.

## Pros

* Incredibly fast setup and learning curve
* Best-in-class soft reserve integration
* Auto-trade feature is genuinely life-changing
* Trade timers prevent costly mistakes
* Works great without requiring raid-wide installation

## Cons

* Less structured than RCLootCouncil for complex decisions
* Voting system isn’t as robust
* History tracking is more basic
* Some features require master looter (Classic only)
* Less suitable for pure loot council systems

## Best For

Guilds running soft reserve, pug-friendly raids, GDKP runs, casual guilds that want simplicity, and any group that values speed over complex decision frameworks.

## Head to Head Comparison
| Feature | RCLootCouncil | Gargul | | — — — — -| — — — — — — — -| — — — — | | Setup Time | 30–60 minutes | 5–10 minutes | | Learning Curve | Moderate to Steep | Easy | | Soft Reserve Support | Limited | Excellent | | Loot Council Voting | Excellent | Basic | | History Tracking | Comprehensive | Adequate | | Auto-Trade | No | Yes | | Trade Timers | No | Yes | | Requires Raid Installation | Yes for full features | No | | Best For | Serious LC Guilds | SR/Casual Guilds |

## Which Addon Wins for Different Scenarios

## Progression Raiding Guild

Winner: RCLootCouncil

When you’re pushing mythic content or Classic hard modes, every piece of gear matters. You need to funnel items to players who will provide the most raid benefit. RCLootCouncil’s structured voting and detailed tracking make these decisions defensible and data-driven.

## Casual Weekly Raid Team

Winner: Gargul
If your guild raids once or twice a week and just wants to have fun, Gargul’s simplicity is perfect. Set up soft reserve, import the sheet, and let people roll. No drama, no complex systems, just loot distributed fairly and quickly.

## Pug Raids

Winner: Gargul

You can’t expect random players to install and configure RCLootCouncil. Gargul works even if you’re the only one with it installed. The roll tracking captures standard /roll commands, and soft reserve integration means pugs can participate through the website without any addon.

## Guild With Loot Drama History

Winner: RCLootCouncil

If your guild has had issues with favoritism accusations or loot disputes, RCLootCouncil’s transparency features are essential. The voting record shows exactly who voted for what, and the history log proves that loot has been distributed fairly over time.

## Classic WoW Raids

Winner: Gargul (slight edge)

With master looter still available in Classic, Gargul’s automation features really shine.
The packmule system, auto-trade, and direct softres.it integration make it the smoother experience. That said, hardcore Classic guilds still swear by RCLootCouncil for progression.

## Setup Walkthrough for Both Addons

## Setting Up RCLootCouncil

1. Install via CurseForge or your preferred addon manager
2. Type /rc config to open settings
3. Configure your council members under the Council tab
4. Customize response buttons to match your loot rules
5. Set up auto-pass rules for armor types your class can’t use
6. Test with your council before raid night

Pro tip: Create a “Test Mode” session before your first raid to let council members practice voting without pressure.

## Setting Up Gargul

1. Install via CurseForge
2. Before raid, have your soft reserve sheet locked on softres.it
3. Click “Gargul Export” on the soft reserve page
4. In-game, click the Gargul minimap icon
5. Select Soft Reserve and paste the copied data
6. Click Import — you’re done

...

Here’s the honest truth: I use both addons, just for different purposes.

For my main guild’s progression team, RCLootCouncil is non-negotiable. The structured voting system has eliminated almost all loot drama, and the history tracking means I can pull up data instantly when someone feels slighted.

For alt raids, pugs, and casual content, Gargul wins every time. The soft reserve integration is flawless, the auto-trade feature is genuinely brilliant, and I can set up an entire loot system in under a minute.

If I had to pick just one? For most players in 2026, Gargul is the better choice. The majority of raids use soft reserve or simple roll systems, and Gargul handles those scenarios with less friction. RCLootCouncil is the superior tool for its specific use case, but that use case — dedicated loot council progression guilds — represents a smaller portion of the player base.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use both addons at the same time? Yes, but there’s no real reason to.
Pick the one that matches your loot system and stick with it.

Does everyone in my raid need to install the addon? For Gargul, no — it works fine if only the master looter has it. For RCLootCouncil, council members need it installed, but regular raiders can function without it.

Which addon works better for retail WoW? RCLootCouncil has better retail support since personal loot changes made master looter less common. Gargul is primarily designed for Classic.

Can Gargul handle loot council decisions? It has basic support, but if you’re running a true loot council, RCLootCouncil is purpose-built for that workflow.

How do I handle someone who claims the addon “glitched”? Both addons maintain logs. Check the history before entertaining complaints.

Is there a way to export loot data to spreadsheets? Yes, both addons support data export. RCLootCouncil has more robust export options.

What happens if the master looter disconnects mid-raid? Both addons store data locally.
